text:
marta: Heads-up — deploybot queued a patch bump for tonight's stable window. Change looks like buildmeta/CI stamp only. Should we let it go to stable or skip?

deploybot: deploybot: Release job queued -> tag candidate: v1.4.2+deploy.2026-03-21 (sha: abc123). Scheduled to promote to stable at 22:00 UTC.

jen: If it's only build metadata we usually skip a semver patch. Last sprint we added an auto-bump rule for any non-empty buildmeta, and it's noisy.

kevin: I agree with skipping. No user-facing change, no release notes. Only downside is some downstream scripts look for monotonic tags.

sam: For downstream hermeticity we could create an internal-only annotated tag (not on stable) like `v1.4.2-ci.20260321` and keep stable at v1.4.1. That preserves monotonicity without exposing a meaningless patch.

marta: I'm leaning to let deploybot do it — ops wants consistent promotion and the releasebot catalog will reflect the build. But I'm OK to defer if ops says skip.

jen: Important: we avoid `+` in canonical tags for packaging ecosystems (npm, pypi). If we create a tag with plus, some consumers choke. So better to either a) no tag, b) semver patch without plus, or c) internal tag with safe separator.

ops-bot: ops-bot: Rollback policy reminder: automatic rollback to prior stable if >5% 5xx or latency spike detected within the first 15m. Manual rollback otherwise.

kevin: Vote check: skip stable bump = sam, jen, kevin. Allow bump = marta. Anyone else?

marta: I don't strongly object to skip. If skipping, can we annotate the CI run in release notes so audit shows it was considered?

jen: I'll cancel the deploybot job and add a release note stub: "build metadata only — no stable bump; CI run recorded".

deploybot: deploybot: Release job canceled by @jen — reason=buildmeta-only; tag_not_created.

marta: Thanks. Please put the stub under drafts/releases/v1.4.x/ so PMs can see it.

jen: Will do. Command I ran: ```deploybot cancel 7043219876 --reason "buildmeta only"```

sam: Leaving a quick ops note: if we later need to force a patch (eg. security backport), we should create a clean `v1.4.2` tag and go through canary first.

kevin: Agreed. Closing thread unless anyone objects. :thumbsup:
